deals.evidence: Reynolds and Mac – previously known as McElhenney – completed their takeover in February 2021 with a £2m investment.
deals.headline: Reynolds and McElhenney take over Wrexham from the Supporters Trust
deals.summary: The actors completed their takeover from the fan-owned Wrexham Supporters Trust with an initial £2m investment; Companies House records them as persons with significant control from 9 February 2021.

deals.evidence: Wrexham have sold a minority club stake to the Allyn family
deals.headline: Wrexham sell minority stake to the Allyn family
deals.summary: The Allyn family of Skaneateles, New York (former owners of Welch Allyn) invested through Red Dragon Ventures LLC, run by family office CIO Eric Allyn; BBC later put the stake at around 15%. Price not disclosed.

deals.evidence: a share issue in March 2025 close to the deal brought in about £14m
deals.headline: Share issue raises about £14m
deals.summary: A share issue in March 2025, close to the Allyn deal, brought in about £14m (BBC gives the figure as approximate).

deals.evidence: A separate share issue in September saw £7m invested.
deals.headline: Further £7m share issue
deals.summary: A separate share issue in September 2025 raised £7m.

deals.date_text: Reported 3 December 2025 (council charge over the stadium registered 17 September 2025)
deals.evidence: A decision to give £18m of public money to Wrexham AFC has been defended by Wrexham council and the Welsh government
deals.headline: £18m public grant for the new Kop stand
deals.investor: Welsh Government and Wrexham County Borough Council
deals.summary: Non-repayable grants of £18m from the Welsh Government and Wrexham council towards the Kop redevelopment and stadium upgrades for international football, with conditions attached; the council registered a charge over the stadium freehold on 17 September 2025.

deals.evidence: have received £47.83m via a new share issue
deals.headline: Apollo Sports Capital takes a minority stake in Wrexham
deals.summary: Apollo's sports arm (also majority owner of Atletico Madrid) took a minority shareholding, believed to be just under 10%, with a board seat and possible further capital for the stadium; Companies House documents confirmed £47.83m received via a new share issue. Reynolds and Mac keep control.

deals.headline: Premier League Stadium Fund charge over the Racecourse freehold
deals.summary: Charge 0769 8872 0003 created 13 July 2026 in favour of Premier League Stadium Fund Limited over the Racecourse Ground freehold (outstanding); amount not stated on the register page.

chair.evidence: Wrexham co-chairmen McElhenney and Reynolds said
chair.name: Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney
chair.title: Co-chairmen

operating_result.basis: operating loss (BBC: 'losses', which it says include promotion bonuses and a £3.76m Argentex write-off)
operating_result.evidence: losses rose significantly from £2m in 2023-24 to £14.85m last season

revenue_breakdown.evidence: Sponsorship - £17,336,378, up from £13,181,133, an increase of 31.5%.
revenue_breakdown.source_name: BBC Sport, 2024-25 revenue split from the accounts (commercial = sponsorship; other = retail)

stadium_owner.detail: Wrexham AFC Limited holds the Racecourse Ground freehold, charged in September 2025 to Wrexham County Borough Council and in July 2026 to the Premier League Stadium Fund; a 2022 charge to the Football Stadia Improvement Fund was over a leasehold title. A new Kop stand (about 7,500 seats) is due to take capacity past 18,000.
stadium_owner.evidence: The freehold property being the racecourse ground

wages.evidence: also show wages leapt up by 73.6% from the previous year to £19.95m

founded_evidence: Wrexham played their first match, against the Prince of Wales Fire Brigade, at Stok Cae Ras on 22 October, 1864
name: Wrexham Association Football Club
notes: Country corrected to Wales. Founded year is from the club's first match (22 October 1864) as BBC Sport states it; no club page with a founding date could be fetched (wrexhamafc.co.uk is a JavaScript app with no fetchable text). The full accounts for the year to 30 June 2025 (Companies House 07698872, filed 27 Mar 2026) are a scanned PDF, so revenue, wages, loss and the revenue split are cited from BBC Sport's report of them; BBC does not say whether the £14.85m loss is operating or pre-tax. PSC register lists Reynolds and Rob Mac each with 75% or more (control band, exact split not stated). The Allyn stake is given only as 'around 15%' and Apollo's as 'believed to be just shy of 10%'; the share issues of ~£14m (Mar 2025), £7m (Sep 2025) and £47.83m (Apollo) are recorded as stated. Valuation is BBC's 'around £350m' citing US reports before the Apollo deal. Current stadium capacity is reduced while the Kop is rebuilt and no current figure was found; the new Kop takes it past 18,000. Shirt sponsor and kit supplier not sourced (BBC names United Airlines and HP as partners without saying which is on the shirt). No dated follower counts found.

owners.evidence: The New York-based Allyn family came on board in 2024, taking a stake of around 15%.
owners.name: Allyn family (Red Dragon Ventures LLC)

owners.evidence: have taken a minority shareholding in the Stok Cae Ras club, believed to be just shy of 10%
owners.name: Apollo Sports Capital

ownership_summary: Wrexham AFC Limited is controlled by co-chairmen Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac (formerly McElhenney), who took over from the Wrexham Supporters Trust in February 2021 with a £2m investment and remain majority owners. The Allyn family office (via Red Dragon Ventures LLC) bought a minority stake of around 15% in October 2024, and Apollo Sports Capital took a minority stake (reported as just under 10%) in December 2025, with £47.83m raised in a new share issue.
revenue_evidence: The club's latest financial figures showed their revenues jumped by almost a quarter to £33.3m while still in League One.
revenue_source_name: BBC Sport on Wrexham AFC Limited accounts for the year ended 30 June 2025

stadium_owner.detail: Wrexham AFC Limited holds the Racecourse Ground freehold, charged in September 2025 to Wrexham County Borough Council and in July 2026 to the Premier League Stadium Fund; a 2022 charge to the Football Stadia Improvement Fund was over a leasehold title. A new Kop stand (about 7,500 seats) is due to take capacity past 18,000.
stadium_owner.evidence: The freehold property being the racecourse ground

valuation_evidence: the value of the club, which now stands at around £350m
valuation_source_name: BBC Sport (citing US reports before the Apollo deal)
